name: Beechcraft Travel Air (95)
summary: Small four-seat twin developed from the Bonanza and built 1958–1968; it was the direct ancestor of the Baron.

wings: Plain wingtips with no tip tanks
engines: Two small Lycoming engines in slim nacelles
fuselage: Compact four-seat cabin with a rounded, Bonanza-style profile

tellTales: Tall, upright, square-topped fin on a compact twin
Small four-seat Bonanza-like cabin with a sloping nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The Baron has a swept-back fin and a larger cabin with bigger engines; the Travel Air has a tall, upright, squared-off fin and is smaller.
The Twin Comanche has a raked fin and an untapered wing; the Travel Air has an upright fin and a tapered wing.
The 310 has large wingtip tanks and a swept fin; the Travel Air has plain tips and an upright fin.
